gogpt_prior_assessment: GOGPT prior names 'Shenzhen Energy East power station' (5,000 MW, gogpt_captive already False, 1.99 km away). A 5-gigawatt station is a regional grid asset far larger than any plausible captive load for a 4 mtpa import terminal, and its scale/generic proximity match (same plant is also flagged for two OTHER Shenzhen-area terminals in this shard at 2.54 km and 7.63 km) indicates GOGPT's proximity algorithm matched the nearest large utility plant to all nearby LNG sites rather than a real captive relationship. Shenzhen Energy does hold 30% equity in this specific terminal, which is more plausibly a gas-OFFTAKE relationship (the terminal may supply regasified gas to Shenzhen Energy's generation fleet) than a captive-power-INTO-the-terminal relationship — a direction-test case worth flagging to a future PowerPlantsSupplied review. I could not locate an independent, citable, non-gem.wiki page specifically describing the East power station within the research budget (web search was exhausted before I could pursue this further).
gogpt_candidate_basis: Existing large utility station, not a dedicated captive plant for this terminal; proximity-only match repeated across three unrelated terminals in this shard is itself evidence against a real captive relationship.
status_or_other_findings: Shenzhen Energy's 30% equity stake in this terminal is a plausible PowerPlantsSupplied-direction lead (terminal may feed Shenzhen Energy's plants) rather than a captive-power lead; flag for the Update workflow, not acted on here.
notes: Web search budget was exhausted partway through this shard (shared session-wide budget); remaining research on this and later terminals relied on WebFetch only, which failed on most Chinese government/portal domains (403s and DNS failures).
